newsitem.title: FINLAND: Miners see zinc remaining in deficit.
newsitem.headline: Miners see zinc remaining in deficit.

text.p: Zinc is likely to remain in deficit for some time to come while copper's long-forecast supply surge remains a trickle, miners said on Wednesday on the sidelines of a metal conference.
"This is a cyclical business and you can already see in the market zinc is on the uptrend due to under-investment in the early 1990," said Anders Bulow, president and CEO of Boliden Ltd.

"The market has been in deficit and we envisage it's going to be in deficit for a period of time," he said at the Metal Bulletin base metal concentrates conference, noting that Boliden was looking to expand its mining and smelting operations in both zinc and copper.
Asko Ojanen, president of Outokumpu Base Metals Oy of Finland, also said zinc looked promising for producers.
"Zinc will seen two really good years, in terms of consumption and price," Ojanen said. But he noted that zinc smelting capacity worldwide was limited.
With regard to copper, Bulow said fresh capacity coming onstream would eventually pressure the copper price, but that had yet to happen.

"My view is that we won't see the great imbalances people were talking if we go back a year. As the new capacity is being delayed we're having a cumulative effect of growth in demand, which means the gap is not going to be as great as originally foreseen," Bulow said.
Boliden was being sought after by copper producers with regard to copper smelting capacity because of new production expected to emerge in the next three to five years, he added.
"People are concerned about finding a home for their copper concentrate," he said.
But Outokumpu's Ojanen said smelting capacity for copper was unlikely to run into too much tightness.
"I'm pretty sure there's enough smelter capacity. It has been said for many years we will have too much copper concentrate. But where is it?" he said.
